data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is defensible only if we accept a 'critical rationalist' definition of rationality that divorces it from justification entirely, viewing the preference for corroborated theories as the only non-arbitrary option remaining after all others have been critically eliminated.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the set of possible theories is infinite, making elimination incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'non-arbitrary' implicitly relies on an inductive assumption that the eliminated patterns won't recur.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If this negative definition of rationality is too weak to guide actual technological application.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Redefines rationality not as 'having positive reasons/beliefs' (which leads to induction) but as 'avoiding error.' It is the 'last man standing' approach.
